correctness.rationale: The semi-Pell recurrence telescopes to u(2m+1)=1+2 sum_{k=1}^m u(k), and its previous modulo-four layer yields a parity count A(m) with exact binary recursions. Induction proves the Q(m) high-bit formula for all m. The two-state sign transfer has T^T T=2I and T^4=-4I, proving the displayed rational Walsh generating functions and all dyadic census formulas. Its orthogonal scaled action bounds signed sums on any aligned dyadic block by 2^(k/2); binary decomposition and the even-odd recurrence establish O(sqrt N) for every cutoff. The explicit subsequence N=2^(4a+1) yields discrepancy of size asymptotic to sqrt N for each residue separately, establishing sharpness. The standalone stdlib verifier checked 65,535 recurrence values, 32,768 Q-formulas, 16 exact dyadic censuses and the transfer identities; finite tests supplement, not replace, the proof. All variable ranges and endpoints include N=1 and r=1.

value.rationale: Modulo-four classification is a known natural arithmetic feature of this classical self-similar sequence. The theorem resolves the first genuinely nontrivial higher 2-adic layer for every index using a compact adjacent-bit statistic, determines all four exact dyadic frequency counts, proves equal natural densities for every cutoff, and shows optimal individual square-root fluctuations. The sharp transition from easy mod-four periodicity to a quadratic binary carry law is mathematically structural and motivates extension to higher moduli. This is a complete infinite classification rather than a routine finite table.
